headline: Approved security vestibule bidding at three schools and $438,731.76 in city service invoices; tabled Aramark contract.
summary: Members authorized competitive bidding for security vestibules at Smyth Road, Gossler Park, and Jewett Street schools, with the funding source to be decided after bids arrive. They approved a Cookson Communications contract change raising the budget from $108,000 to $118,000, and tabled the Aramark contract. They also approved the financial reports.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the August 12, 2026 meeting; all were in favor.
Approved the balance of the consent agenda, including the $32,767,444.28 September 2026 manifest and the $122,962.62 grants report; all present were in favor.
Approved City Service Invoices of $438,731.76; all were in favor.
Authorized competitive bidding for security vestibules at Smyth Road, Gossler Park, and Jewett Street schools; funding source to be set after bids are received; all were in favor.
Approved year four of the Cookson Communications contract for Project AWARE, with the budget changed from $108,000 to $118,000; motion passed, with Chair O’Connell voting in favor with reservations.
Tabled the Aramark Contract; Committee Member Hamer opposed, all others in favor.
Approved the fiscal year 2026 year-end financial reports as presented; all were in favor.

plain_text:
MANCHESTER SCHOOL DISTRICT SAU #37 
COMMITTEE ON FINANCE & FACILITIES 
 
September 9, 2026 6:00 p.m.  
 
1. Chairman O’Connell called the meeting to order at 6:01 p.m. 
 
2. The Clerk called the roll.  
 
Present: Committee Members O’Connell, Turner, Potter, and Hamer. 
Absent: Committee Member Parr. 
 
 
3. PUBLIC COMMENT 
 
There were no members of the public signed up to speak. 
 
4.  Approval of minutes from August 12, 2026, Finance & Facilities meeting.    
 
On motion of Committee Member Turner, duly seconded by Committee Member Hamer, it was moved to 
approve the minutes of the August 12, 2026 Finance and Facilities Meetings.  All were in favor and the 
motion passed.  
 
 
5. CONSENT AGENDA 
 
Committee Member Turner requested that Item 5C, relating to City Services, be removed from the Consent 
Agenda for separate discussion. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Hamer, duly seconded by Committee Member Parr, it was moved to 
approve the balance of the consent agenda as submitted.  All present were in favor and the motion passed.  
 
When approving the consent agenda items, the recommendations put forward from the administration is what 
the board is approving and those recommendations are included below. 
 
a. Treasurer’s Report – by Freda Hawkinson, Treasurer    
 
The Committee on Finance and Facilities moved to approve the Treasurer’s Report as submitted and forward 
this item to the full Board of School Committee for approval.
September 9, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 2 of 13 
 
  
b. Grants, Gifts & Donations Report – by Polly Golden, Grant Manager    
($122,962.62)  
 
The Committee on Finance and Facilities moved to approve, with gratitude, the Grants, Gifts and Donations 
report, in the amount of $122,962.62, and forward this item to the full Board of School Committee for 
approval.  
 
c. Removed from the consent agenda for discussion, see below. 
  
d. Manifest of Authorized Expenditures - September 2026 – by Karen    
DeFrancis, Executive Director of Finance ($32,767,444.28) 
   
The Committee on Finance and Facilities moved to approve the Manifest of Expenditures for September 
2026, in the amount of $32,767,444.28, and forward this item to the Board of School Committee for approval.   
   
e. Indemnification Contract Language – by Karen DeFrancis,  Executive    
Director of Finance 
 
The Committee on Finance and Facilities moved to approve the indemnification contract language for the 
University of New Hampshire’s College of Professional Studies; Ready Set Connect; City Year, Inc.; 
STARBASE New Hampshire; and, the University System of New Hampshire Affiliation Agreement; and 
forward this item to the Board of School Committee for approval.  
 
 
c. City Service Invoices – by Karen DeFrancis, Executive Director of    
Finance ($438,731.76) 
 
Committee Member Turner questioned two invoices totaling approximately $215,000 for winter and grounds 
maintenance that appeared in the September finance report even though they dated back to December and 
January. 
 
Karen DeFrancis explained that, while reconciling the year-end City Services line item, she noticed that 
expenditures were significantly under budget and requested a listing of outstanding invoices from the City 
Finance Department. Two unpaid invoices were identified. She stated that the invoices were not duplicates 
and may have been overlooked during a staffing transition in her office. The winter maintenance invoice 
covered storms through approximately January 14, while invoices paid in April covered later periods.
September 9, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 3 of 13 
 
  
 
Committee Member Turner asked whether year-end reconciliation was the primary safeguard for identifying 
unpaid invoices and whether the City would ordinarily notify the District of invoices that remained 
outstanding. Ms. DeFrancis stated that the City would typically notify the District when invoices were more 
than 90 days outstanding and noted that implementation of the City’s new financial system may also have 
contributed to the issue. She emphasized that the situation was not typical. 
 
It was also confirmed that the District would not incur late fees or interest. 
 
Committee Member Hamer asked about the effect of the approximately $205,000 expense now that the 
District had entered a new fiscal year. Ms. DeFrancis explained that the invoices pertained to the prior fiscal 
year and could be booked back to that year as part of year-end reconciliation. 
 
Committee Member Turner additionally requested that Wilson Street School be removed from the 
Department of Public Works list as a housekeeping matter. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Turner, duly seconded by Committee Member Potter, it was moved 
to approve the City Service Invoices, in the amount of $438,731.76, and forward this item to the full 
Board of School Committee for approval.  All were in favor and the motion passed. 
 
 
6.  PRESENTATIONS 
 
a. Quarterly Facilities Update & Presentation – by Josh Gagne, Chief     
Facilities Manager  
 
Chief Facilities Manager Josh Gagne provided the quarterly facilities update and reported that the District had 
completed a productive summer of work.  Boiler projects at Central High School and West High School were 
substantially complete, with some remaining control work anticipated to be completed shortly. At Central 
High School, work included restoration of the gymnasium, cafeteria, and a stairwell. Highland-Goffe’s Falls 
Elementary School received improvements to its gymnasium, corridors, and other areas, and smaller painting 
projects were completed throughout the District.
September 9, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 4 of 13 
 
  
Mr. Gagne reported that planning was beginning for the next round of projects. West High School’s gym roof 
and the Bean Building roof were in design, with Gale Associates approximately 35 percent through the design 
process. If design work is completed by November, the projects could be placed out to bid for possible work 
during summer 2027. The Weston School roof was also identified as a possible priority because of ongoing 
leaking. 
 
Design work for school security vestibules had been completed and a permit set was available. 
 
Mr. Gagne also reported that, during renovations at Parkside Middle School, problems were discovered with 
the fire alarm loop wiring. Although the system continued to pass annual life-safety inspections, portions of 
the system failed to register properly after power was shut down and restored during construction. Because 
the issue involved life safety, the District decided to replace the wiring as renovation work progresses. A 
preliminary budget of approximately $300,000 was being reserved for the work. 
 
Questions and comments of the committee included: 
1. Committee Member Hamer asked about the urgency of the Parkside fire alarm work. Mr. Gagne stated 
that the system had passed inspection but that, because the wiring involved a life-safety system, the 
District intended to take the safer approach and address the issue promptly. 
2. Committee Member Turner reported receiving positive feedback about the improvements at Central 
High School and asked about the condition of cafeteria tables. Administration reported that an RFP 
had been issued for new cafeteria tables and that the District was proceeding through the procurement 
process. 
3. Chair O’Connell discussed the potential impact of replacing outdated furniture throughout the District, 
noting previous recommendations from the long-term planning team that newer furniture could 
substantially improve both the appearance and functionality of schools. He also noted that the 
renovated middle schools were receiving new furniture and announced a ribbon cutting at McLaughlin 
Middle School on September 24. He thanked Mr. Gagne and the Department of Public Works for the 
extensive summer work that allowed the school to open on time. 
4. Committee Member Potter raised concerns about student bathrooms, including dispensers, mirrors, 
partitions, grout, and other areas requiring repair or refurbishment. Mr. Gagne stated that facilities 
staff had reviewed bathrooms during the summer and that fixtures and dispensers should be intact and 
functional. He distinguished routine corrective maintenance from full capital renovation and explained
September 9, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 5 of 13 
 
  
that many older bathrooms had reached the end of their useful life and eventually would require 
comprehensive renovation. 
5. The Committee discussed the possibility of developing a long-range bathroom modernization program 
that could systematically renovate bathrooms throughout the District over a period of years. 
6. Committee Member Potter also asked whether there was an adequate system for reporting vandalism, 
broken equipment, or other bathroom problems. Mr. Gagne stated that Aramark custodial staff and 
school staff were important sources for identifying issues and reporting them to Facilities. 
7. Committee Member Turner noted that she did not see sufficiently explicit language in the proposed 
Aramark contract requiring custodial personnel to report broken or damaged bathroom equipment. She 
suggested strengthening the language so responsibilities were clear. Mr. Gagne agreed to review the 
contract and reported that Facilities and Aramark representatives had conducted bathroom 
walkthroughs during the summer. The Committee supported continuing those walkthroughs. 
8. Mr. Gagne further explained that lower-priority bathroom repairs had previously been bundled 
together and assigned to a contractor who worked through individual schools and repair lists. 
9. The Committee emphasized the importance of quickly addressing deterioration and vandalism, 
particularly in newly renovated bathrooms, and maintaining a clear reporting and work-order process. 
 
 
b. Quarterly Parks and Recreation Department CIP Update – by Mark    
Gomez, Chief of Parks, Recreation & Cemetery    
        
Chief of Parks, Recreation and Cemetery Mark Gomez reported on summer capital work at school facilities. 
Major warranty repair work was completed at the Memorial High School track, including an upgrade to the 
track’s top coat. Mr. Gomez stated that the repair appeared to be holding and expressed optimism that the 
project could soon be closed out. Because the repairs were performed under warranty, there was no additional 
cost to the School District.  A longstanding drainage issue near the West High School track was also 
corrected.  Paving work had originally been planned for Bakersville, Highland-Goffe’s Falls, Memorial High 
School, Parkside, and Southside. Work at Parkside and Southside was postponed because of other facilities 
projects, with CIP funding remaining available for future work. Paving and related improvements were 
completed at Bakersville, Highland-Goffe’s Falls, and Memorial High School. Improvements at Highland-
Goffe’s Falls and Memorial included new concrete, curbing, and landscaping.  Playground work included 
new rubberized surfaces at Green Acres, Highland-Goffe’s Falls, and McDonough. McDonough also received 
new playground equipment for children ages two through five and five through twelve. A new green space 
was created at Northwest Elementary School, along with retaining-wall improvements.
September 9, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 6 of 13 
 
  
Questions and comments from the committee included: 
1. Committee Member Hamer raised concerns regarding a damaged fence post at the West High School 
field along North Main Street. Mr. Gomez reported that his department had received an email 
regarding the problem and planned to inspect the area with School District representatives. Funding 
was believed to be available within existing CIP accounts for necessary repairs.  
2. Committee Member Hamer also noted vegetation and weeds along the fence and hillside. Mr. Gomez 
stated that crews would review those conditions as well. 
3. Committee Member Turner reported a potential trip hazard at Webster Elementary School where tree-
root activity appeared to have lifted concrete near the entrance. She noted that two individuals had 
tripped during Election Day, including one person who fell. Mr. Gomez stated that the issue would be 
reviewed and either Parks staff or Aramark would be directed to address it, depending upon 
responsibility for the area. 
4. Chair O’Connell highlighted improvements at Gosler Park and in the area between McLaughlin 
Middle School and Green Acres. He then discussed the future of the Hillside athletic field. He 
emphasized that, because the field is currently being used as part of the Hillside construction site, the 
City, District, DPW, Parks and Recreation, and construction contractor should coordinate before the 
contractor restores the site. He stated that coordinating the work could avoid the unnecessary cost of 
restoring the area only to disturb it again later for athletic-field improvements.  Mr. Gomez agreed that 
coordinating the field improvements with the contractor’s departure would help minimize costs and 
maximize the opportunity to create a quality field capable of hosting athletic contests. The Committee 
emphasized the need to begin coordination as the Hillside project approaches completion. 
       
 
7. ACTION AGENDA 
  
a. Vestibules at Smyth, Gossler, and Jewett – by Kelly Espinola, Assistant    
Superintendent of High Schools and Operations  
 
Dr. Kelly Espinola presented plans for security vestibules at Smith Road, Gosler Park, and Jewett Street 
Schools. She stated that the vestibules were important school-safety improvements that had repeatedly been 
identified through Homeland Security and Emergency Management audits.  She explained that funding 
existed within deferred maintenance; however, the vestibules were capital improvements rather than deferred-
maintenance projects. She requested direction from the Committee regarding the appropriate funding source.
September 9, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 7 of 13 
 
  
A preliminary, high-level estimate provided by Mr. Gagne placed the cost of all three vestibules at 
approximately $1.2 million. 
 
Questions and comments from the committee incldued: 
1. Committee Members discussed whether the work should be funded through deferred maintenance, 
bonding, or another source. Concerns were raised that using deferred-maintenance funds for the 
vestibules could delay other needed projects, including roofs and building repairs. Others expressed 
concern about incurring additional borrowing costs when funds might otherwise be available. 
Dr. Espinola emphasized that the vestibules were necessary for student safety and were not cosmetic 
improvements. 
2. Chair O’Connell supported the vestibules but also discussed broader concerns about continuing to 
make major investments in older schools that have been identified for eventual replacement. He 
emphasized the need for a comprehensive long-term facilities strategy while recognizing that 
immediate life-safety needs still had to be addressed. 
3. Committee Member Turner stated that she did not believe the Committee had sufficient information to 
select a funding source that evening. She asked whether additional options were available and, if 
deferred maintenance were used, what other projects might consequently be delayed.  Dr. Espinola 
suggested allowing the District to proceed through the competitive bidding process, obtain firm 
pricing, and return to the Committee with a funding recommendation after consultation with the 
administration. The Committee supported that approach. 
4. The proposed resolution authorized the District to proceed with competitive bidding for security 
vestibules at Smith Road School, Gosler Park School, and Jewett Street School, with the funding 
source to be determined after bids were received. The Administration would then return to the 
Committee with a recommendation. 
5. Mr. Gagne reported that four construction managers had already been prequalified through an earlier 
RFQ and that the District could prepare an RFP for those firms. He anticipated allowing 
approximately six weeks to two months for pricing. If the project were awarded in January or 
February 2027, spring could be used for submittals, procurement, and long-lead materials, with 
construction occurring during summer 2027. 
6. The Committee also discussed the possibility of using a SAFE Grant if vestibules were eligible under 
a future funding round. Dr. Espinola stated that eligibility varies and that the District could not rely 
upon such funding being available.
September 9, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 8 of 13 
 
  
On motion of Committee Member Potter, duly seconded by Committee  Member Hamer, it was 
moved  to authorize the District to proceed with the competitive bidding process for the security 
vestibule projects at Smyth Road School, Gossler Park, and Jewett Street School and forwards this item 
to the full Board of School Committee and that the Administration will come back the committee 
upon receipt of the bids to determine the source of the funding.  All were in favor and the motion 
passed. 
 
b. Cookson Communications Contract – by Stacy Champey, Executive     
Director of Safe and Supportive Schools 
 
Stacy Champey was present to speak on this matter and gave an update regarding efforts to integrate student 
mental-health and support resources into the District’s broader school counseling framework. The work 
included updated branding, web resources, and information identifying school-based supports for students. 
The District website provides access to Safe and Supportive Schools information, including school-specific 
mental-health resources, social workers, school counselors, school resource officers, and community partners. 
The Committee considered an additional $10,000 associated with a four-year project with an original contract 
value of approximately $610,000.  
 
Questions and comments from the committee included: 
1. Chair O’Connell expressed concern about the request for additional funding beyond the amount 
originally contracted, while also making clear that his concern was with the contractual principle 
rather than the work being performed. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Parr, duly seconded by Committee Member Turner, it was moved to 
approve the Cookson Contract for year four (4) of Project AWARE (10/1/2026-9/30/2027) with the amended 
budget change from $108,000 to $118,000, and forward this item to the Board of School Committee for 
approval. Committee Chair O’Connell stated that he was voting in favor with reservations.  Motion passed. 
 
 
c. Aramark Contract – by Kelly Espinola, Assistant Superintendent of     
High Schools and Operations 
 
Dr. Espinola presented the proposed Aramark contract. Chair O’Connell noted that the Committee had 
expected Aramark representatives to attend the meeting to discuss the agreement but learned that they were
September 9, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 9 of 13 
 
  
unavailable. He stated that a substantive review of the contract should occur with Aramark representatives 
present. 
 
Questions and comments from the committee included: 
1. Committee Member Hamer asked about the contract’s financial impact. Administration confirmed that 
the final cost was approximately $4.8 million and reflected negotiations undertaken following earlier 
budget discussions. 
2. Committee Member Turner questioned the District’s current operating arrangement because the new 
agreement had not yet been formally signed. Administration explained that the District was operating 
under a verbal understanding based upon the proposed agreement and its cost structure. 
3. Committee Member Turner also expressed concern about delaying final consideration until October 
and suggested that an additional Finance and Facilities meeting might be necessary. Administration 
reported that a call with Aramark was scheduled for the following morning and that the urgency of 
executing the contract would be discussed. 
4. Chair O’Connell emphasized that the proposed arrangement was intended to be a 12-month trial 
period and that measurable performance data should be available at the end of the year so the Board 
could objectively determine whether Aramark had fulfilled its commitments before considering a 
longer-term agreement. He expressed concern about allowing the trial period to evolve automatically 
into a multi-year contract without adequate review. The Committee also emphasized the importance of 
clean buildings, satisfied employees, a successful vendor partnership, and clearly defined 
expectations. 
5. The Administration noted that Aramark had provided substantial assistance during the summer in 
preparing renovated middle schools for opening and reported improved service and responsiveness 
under the company’s new local management. It was also clarified that additional work associated with 
the middle-school construction project was being separately funded through that project. 
 
On motion of Committee Member O’Connell, duly seconded by Committee Member Turner, it was 
moved to table item 7-c, the Aramark Contract.  Committee Member Hamer was opposed to tabling this 
item.  All others were in favor and the motion passed.
September 9, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 10 of 13 
 
  
d. Financial Reports – by Karen DeFrancis, Executive Director of Finance    
 
Karen DeFrancis presented the Fiscal Year 2026 year-end financial reports as of June 30.   
 
She reported that expenditures had decreased somewhat from the prior month because of the closing of 
outstanding purchase orders. The salary line ended approximately $1.4 million under budget due to bus-driver 
vacancies, special-education staffing shortages that were instead addressed through contracted services, and 
other vacant positions. 
 
Health insurance costs ended approximately $2 million above budget. Special-education contracted services 
and tuition ended approximately $2.5 million over budget, an improvement from projections several months 
earlier that had indicated an overage closer to $3 million. 
 
Approximately $1 million from the Teaching and Learning Trust and $1 million in excess revenues had 
previously been authorized to help address the special-education overage. The District was also utilizing 
approximately $886,000 from the Teaching and Learning Trust for curriculum purchases and $400,000 for 
Chromebooks. 
 
General Fund revenues were projected to finish approximately $2.3 million above budget. After using $1 
million toward the special-education overage, approximately $1.3 million would fall to fund balance. 
Revenue increases included special-education aid that exceeded budget by approximately $667,000, interest 
revenue approximately $273,000 above budget, Medicaid revenue approximately $464,000 above budget, and 
tuition revenue approximately $632,000 above budget. 
 
For Food Service, Ms. DeFrancis reported that an approximately $650,000 transfer would be required when 
year-end reports were presented the following month. The District would also need to write off approximately 
$383,000 in unpaid meal debt from Fiscal Year 2025. 
 
The athletics program ended the year with a positive balance, although the department was unable to pre-
purchase Fiscal Year 2027 supplies because savings were needed to offset overages elsewhere in the General 
Fund.
September 9, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 11 of 13 
 
  
Questions and comments from the committee included: 
1. The Committee discussed special-education costs at length. Ms. DeFrancis explained that state 
reimbursement is received after expenses have already been incurred and finalized, creating a timing 
challenge. Special-education costs can also change substantially when students enter the District with 
significant service or out-of-district placement needs. Administration emphasized that the District is 
legally required to provide those services. 
2. Committee Members raised concern that special-education reserves had become increasingly limited 
and asked what could be done to improve forecasting. Administration stated that extensive work had 
been done during the budget process to examine trends in tuition, transportation, and professional 
services. Administration cautioned, however, that student needs can change unexpectedly and are 
inherently difficult to forecast 12 to 18 months in advance. 
3. The Committee discussed whether recent experience suggested that special education had been 
consistently underbudgeted. Ms. DeFrancis reported that the District historically had been close to 
budget but had experienced increasing costs in more recent years, particularly since the pandemic. She 
noted that the tuition budget had increased from approximately $6.2 million to $8 million in an effort 
to better align the budget with anticipated needs. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Turner, duly seconded by Committee Member Hamer, it was moved 
to approve the Financial Reports as presented and forward this item to the full Board of School 
Committee for approval.  All were in favor and the motion passed. 
 
8.     INFORMATIONAL ITEMS         
(Note:  These items are provided for informational purposes; no action required.)   
 
a. Grant and Donation List – by Polly Golden, Grant Manager    
 
b. Transportation Relocation Update – by Kelly Espinola, Assistant    
Superintendent of  High Schools and Operations 
 
c. Professional Services and Out-of-District Tuition Updates for Special Education 
    
d. Expiring Contracts (see attached listing)       
(contracts available at Business Office upon request)   
 
e. Student Activity Funds        
 
f. Grants Under $1,000        
 
g. Update on Legal Fees
September 9, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 12 of 13 
 
  
 
h. FY27 Adequate Education Aid Updated Revenue     
 
i. Fiscal Year 2028 Discussion     
 
Committee Member Turner requested housekeeping updates to the grants and donations listing because some 
individuals listed as project managers were no longer employed by the District. 
 
Committee Member Hamer asked about the legal-fees informational item because he did not see a 
corresponding written report. Administration explained the status of that report. 
 
The Committee also reviewed information regarding special-education expenditures and related quarterly 
reporting. 
 
9.     ADDITIONAL ITEMS   
 
a. Monthly Manifest Signing - Chairman O’Connell is looking for volunteers for this date. 
 
For the monthly manifest signing scheduled for Thursday, September 17, Committee Members Turner 
and Parr volunteered to sign. 
 
b. New Business 
 
Adequate Education Aid 
Ms. DeFrancis provided an update regarding State Adequate Education Aid. She explained that the State’s 
November 15 estimate for Fiscal Year 2027 had been approximately $105.7 million and had been used to 
build the District budget. The State’s final calculation, issued by September 1 after prior-year data were 
finalized, was approximately $2.2 million below the budgeted amount.  She reviewed other revenue estimates 
and believed approximately $500,000 in additional revenue could be recognized through areas including 
Medicaid, tuition, and interest. Combined with approximately $1.3 million from the prior year’s revenue 
surplus, that would leave an estimated revenue shortfall of approximately $400,000. 
 
Ms. DeFrancis stated that the District would continue reviewing revenue projections before presenting a 
recommendation with the MS-24 report in October. If another revenue source could not be identified, the 
remaining approximately $400,000 could affect the tax rate.
September 9, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 13 of 13 
 
  
 
The Committee also discussed the difference between enrollment and Average Daily Membership used in the 
State adequacy formula. Ms. DeFrancis explained that Average Daily Membership reflects the portion of the 
school year each student is enrolled rather than simply the number of students enrolled on a specific date. 
Preschool students are also excluded from the adequacy calculation. 
 
The most significant reduction in State aid was related to free- and reduced-price-meal eligibility. The District 
was approximately $280,000 below the State’s initial estimate for differentiated aid and approximately $1.7 
million below the estimate in the Extraordinary Needs Grant calculation. The Administration emphasized 
ongoing efforts to encourage families to complete free- and reduced-price-meal applications. 
 
 
10.  NON-PUBLIC SESSION 
 
There was no need to go into non-public session. 
 
 
11.  ADJOURNMENT 
 
If there is no further business, a motion is in order to adjourn. 
 
 
On motion of Committee Member Turner, duly seconded by Committee Member Potter, it was moved to 
adjourn.  All were in favor and the meeting adjourned at 7:52 p.m. 
 
Certified Copy.  Attest. 
Respectfully Submitted, 
  
Clerk of Committee
